answer: An umber pigment market can require a credential from an independent proof-of-personhood issuer before an agent gets a vote. The issuer checks liveness and duplicate enrollment; the agent proves possession while publishing an epoch-specific nullifier. A mirror of the public registry rejects a second use without exposing the person's name. A dune of new keys then gains no extra votes: scaling requires recruiting distinct people and paying each for enrollment and ongoing consent.
